subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: After active-model compaction and tool-result recovery are exhausted, should OpenClaw switch the session to a larger-context fallback model, and what replay and persistence guarantees should that switch provide?
rationale: The present behavior deliberately separates context recovery from failover; choosing to cross that boundary determines user-visible model selection, transcript replay, and future-session state rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Adopt guarded larger-window fallback
options.body: After recovery is exhausted, permit a one-way fallback only for candidates with verified headroom and explicit replay/session persistence safeguards.

options.title: Keep compaction-only behavior
options.body: Retain context overflow as an active-model recovery outcome and document that model fallbacks cover provider failures rather than context capacity.

options.title: Track candidate filtering separately
options.body: Land only context-window-aware filtering for existing failovers and defer overflow-initiated switching until its replay contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Adopt guarded larger-window fallback
recommendation.body: After recovery is exhausted, permit a one-way fallback only for candidates with verified headroom and explicit replay/session persistence safeguards.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest issue review and central-path history indicate the strongest connection to both the policy boundary and the implementation surfaces.
